title: Thawing Cryopreserved Cells
purpose: To recover cryopreserved mammalian cell lines with high viability while minimising DMSO toxicity and contamination risk.
principle: Cells frozen in a cryoprotectant such as DMSO are damaged by slow warming and by prolonged DMSO exposure at 37 °C. Rapid warming, immediate dilution in pre-warmed medium and removal of DMSO by gentle centrifugation maximise survival [1][2][3]. Cells are then seeded at the recommended density and checked after 24 h.

materials.detail: To disinfect water bath and vial
Stored in liquid nitrogen vapor phase (below −130 °C)
T-25 or other size per the supplier

steps.text: Pre-warm complete medium to 37 °C, disinfect the water bath, and label flasks and tubes [2].
Put 5–9 mL of medium in a sterile 15 mL tube and pre-equilibrate the culture vessel [1][3].
Wearing a face shield and cryo gloves, remove the vial from liquid nitrogen and check the label [1].
Hold the lower part of the vial in the 37 °C bath, swirling gently with the cap above water, until a small ice crystal remains [1][2][3].
Wipe the vial with 70% ethanol and move it to the biosafety cabinet [1][3].
Transfer the contents slowly (dropwise for sensitive cells) into the tube of warm medium [2].
Centrifuge gently to remove DMSO: 125 × g for 10 min or 200 × g for 3–5 min [1][2][3].
Aspirate the supernatant carefully and resuspend the pellet in fresh pre-warmed medium.
Count cells and assess viability by trypan blue or an automated counter [2][3].
Seed at the recommended density; if none is listed, thaw the whole vial into a T-25 flask [3].
Incubate at 37 °C, 5% CO₂ and check attachment and morphology after about 24 h [1][2].

results: Viability typically well above 70% after thaw for robust cell lines.
Cells attach and show normal morphology within 24 h; hybridomas can need several days.
controls: Count an aliquot before seeding to record post-thaw viability
Keep a non-thawed backup vial from the same lot

troubleshooting.cause: Slow thaw, DMSO exposure, rough pipetting
troubleshooting.fix: Thaw quickly, wash promptly, pipette gently

troubleshooting.cause: Too few viable cells or wrong vessel
troubleshooting.fix: Seed more densely; check coating needs

safety: Liquid nitrogen causes severe cold burns: wear cryo gloves, face shield and lab coat.
Sealed vials can burst on warming; follow your institution's rules.
DMSO penetrates skin; wear gloves. Cells may carry pathogens: follow local biosafety rules.
references: ATCC. Animal Cell Culture Guide (initiating frozen cultures). https://www.atcc.org/resources/culture-guides/animal-cell-culture-guide
